dedupe_keys.name: climate adaptation strategy for the grimsel area guttannen and innertkirchen swiss alps

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the participatory climate adaptation strategy for the Grimsel area, the high mountain municipalities of Guttannen and Innertkirchen in the canton of Berne. Settlements, infrastructure and the road connections are exposed to rock fall, mudflows, torrents, landslides, avalanches and floods from debris aggradation, and permafrost thaw, glacier retreat and heavier rain are expected to make mass movements more likely, also in summer. The strategy was one of 31 pilot projects in the first phase (2013 to 2017) of the Swiss federal pilot programme, which funded them with 7.7 million Swiss francs in total. From 2014 to 2016 a working group led by the Regionalkonferenz Oberland-Ost, with the cantonal engineering office, all municipalities and actors from the energy industry, transport infrastructure, tourism and agriculture, defined strategic directions and fields of action for buildings and facilities, the cantonal road and infrastructure, tourism, economic development and village life; implementation started in 2016. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Coverage is the Grimsel area of Switzerland. Caveats: costs and benefits of measures were not quantified, and several measures were delayed. It illustrates multi-hazard adaptation planning for alpine road access and settlements. outcomes: A participatory regional strategy with four strategic directions and measures for buildings, the cantonal road, tourism, economy and village life was adopted, and a steering group for implementation was set up in 2016.
